name: Brush hair: A person uses a hairbrush or comb to groom their hair, making repeated strokes through the strands.
Cartwheel: A gymnastic move where a person places their hands on the ground and rotates their body sideways in a circular motion, landing on their feet.
Catch: A person receives and holds an object thrown or dropped (e.g., catching a ball, frisbee, or other item) with hands.
Chew: A person moves their jaw repeatedly to break down food in their mouth.
Clap: Hands strike each other, usually repeatedly, producing sound (applause).
Climb: A person ascends a vertical or inclined structure (e.g., wall, tree, ladder, or rock face).
Climb stairs: A person ascends a staircase step by step.
Dive: A person jumps headfirst into water or performs a diving motion into a surface.
Draw sword: A person unsheathes a sword from its scabbard in a deliberate motion.
Dribble: A person repeatedly bounces or controls a ball (commonly a basketball or soccer ball) while moving.
Drink: A person consumes liquid by bringing a cup, bottle, or container to the mouth.
Eat: A person consumes solid food, typically bringing it to the mouth and chewing.
Fall floor: A person loses balance and collapses onto the ground.
Fencing: Two participants engage in a sport duel using swords (foil, épée, or sabre) with protective gear.
Flic flac: A gymnastic back handspring where a person flips backward, pushing off with hands and landing on feet.
Golf: A person swings a golf club to strike a golf ball, typically on a course or practice range.
Handstand: A person balances upside down on their hands, with legs extended upward.
Hit: A person strikes an object or another person using hand, arm, or an object.
Hug: A person wraps arms around another person in an embrace.
Jump: A person propels themselves off the ground with both feet, becoming airborne.
Kick: A person strikes outward with a foot, targeting an object, person, or into open air.
Kick ball: A person strikes a ball with the foot, sending it forward.
Kiss: A person presses their lips against another person (or object) in a gesture of affection or greeting.
Laugh: A person produces vocal and facial expressions of amusement (smiling, chuckling, or loud laughter).
Pick: A person selects or lifts an object, often using fingers or hand (e.g., picking fruit, picking up an item).
Pour: A person tilts a container to transfer liquid into another container.
Pullup: A person grips a horizontal bar and pulls their body upward until the chin passes the bar.
Punch: A person strikes forward with a closed fist.
Push: A person applies force by extending arms to move an object or person away.
Pushup: A person performs an exercise by lowering and raising the body using arms while facing downward on the ground.
Ride bike: A person pedals and balances on a bicycle in motion.
Ride horse: A person sits on and directs a horse in motion.
Run: A person moves quickly on foot, alternating steps at high speed.
Shake hands: Two people grasp each other’s hands and move them slightly up and down in greeting or agreement.
Shoot ball: A person attempts to score by propelling a ball toward a goal/hoop (basketball, soccer, etc.).
Shoot bow: A person pulls back a bowstring and releases an arrow.
Shoot gun: A person fires a firearm by pulling the trigger.
Sit: A person lowers the body onto a surface (chair, bench, floor) with hips supported.
Situp: A person performs an abdominal exercise by rising from a lying to a seated position.
Smile: A person curves the lips upward, often showing pleasure or friendliness.
Smoke: A person inhales or exhales smoke from a cigarette, cigar, or pipe.
Somersault: A person rolls forward or backward over the head and back, either on the ground or in the air.
Stand: A person rises to and maintains an upright position on both feet.
Swing baseball: A person swings a bat in an attempt to hit a baseball.
Sword: A person handles or brandishes a sword in non-sport context (not fencing or exercise).
Sword exercise: A person practices stylized sword movements, often martial arts forms or drills.
Talk: A person engages in spoken communication with others, using mouth movements and gestures.
Throw: A person propels an object through the air by moving the arm and releasing it.
Turn: A person rotates their body or head to change direction.
Walk: A person moves forward step by step at normal pace with alternating feet.
Wave: A person raises and moves their hand (side-to-side or up-and-down) as a greeting or signal.
